cases.description: When the schema has a non‑null id, the method should return true without checking parent schema or locations.
When the id is null and the schema has no parent (root schema), the method should return true.
When the id is null, a parent schema exists, and both the schema and its parent have the same absolute IRI, the method should return false (the schema is not a resource root).
When the id is null, a parent schema exists, and the absolute IRIs differ, the method should return true (the schema is a resource root).
When the schema id is an empty string (non‑null), the method should return true, treating it as a defined id.
When id is null, a parent schema exists, and both the schema and its parent have a null SchemaLocation, Objects.equals(null, null) is true, so the method returns false.

When id is null, a parent schema exists, the schema's SchemaLocation is null while the parent's SchemaLocation has a non‑null absolute IRI, Objects.equals(null, nonNull) is false, thus the method returns true.

When id is null, a parent schema exists, the schema's SchemaLocation has a non‑null absolute IRI but the parent's SchemaLocation is null, Objects.equals(nonNull, null) is false, so the method returns true.
When the schema has a null id, a non‑null parent schema, but the schema's SchemaLocation is null, calling getSchemaLocation().getAbsoluteIri() throws NullPointerException.

When the schema has a null id, a non‑null parent schema whose SchemaLocation is null (while the schema's own SchemaLocation is non‑null), the call to getParentSchema().getSchemaLocation().getAbsoluteIri() throws NullPointerException.
